twitter_thread: Most QA teams spend more time maintaining their test suite than running it. Here's how to fix the structure so maintenance largely takes care of itself. 🧵

Problem: copy-paste steps. When the login flow changes, you update 300 test cases. Solution: shared steps. When the login flow changes, you update one shared step. Every test case that uses it updates automatically.

Problem: inconsistent formats. Some test cases have preconditions, some don't. Some have risk levels, some don't. Solution: templates. Define required fields once. Every test case in the project follows the structure.

Problem: single-dimension organization. Folders organize by feature area. But you also need to filter by risk level, sprint, environment, test type. Solution: tags. A test case can have 5 tags. Filter by any combination.

Problem: test matrix tracking. Same test cases need to run on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, iOS, Android. Solution: configurations. Define your environments once. Track results per configuration in the same run.

Set up templates + shared steps + tags + configurations before writing the first test case. The structural maintenance problem largely disappears. Full guide: testfiesta.com/blog/flexible-test-case-structure
